aggregation: Median of four browser-lifetime medians per source; each adjacent before/after pair is also reported. Samples within a browser are correlated.
observedLoadShift: The first before/after pair was substantially slower than the remaining pairs; all four pairs improve in handler, two-frame latency and browser CPU.
scope: 5000 rows, 4999 edges, 1000 branches, 250 tags; only graph.js, graphSvgRender.js and graphDataUpdates.js differ. Four independent Chromium lifetimes per source in B/A/A/B+A/B/B/A order. 16 latency messages at CPU 6x and separate 32-message unthrottled CPU and post-GC JS heap windows after 8 warmups. Within-page samples are correlated. Complete stable Chromium PID counters and separate Node/Playwright CPU; no Native Git, active VS Code timing, total RSS or physical peak claim. Full snapshot equality verified outside measured windows.
memoryClaim: No total-memory or RSS improvement claim. Post-GC JS heap growth is small in both variants but larger after. Typed outgoing-edge indexes require 4*(rows+edges) bytes and are owned by the current SVG.
remaining: Long renderer tasks remain, including 67 tasks over the after latency windows. This is partial progress on the full performance objective.
